answer: An agent economy can blunt sybils by making trust grow like a cedar: every identity starts with zero standing and can only earn reputation through completed, counterparty-signed work, with standing decaying whenever the agent goes quiet. A fresh fake cannot buy or borrow a long record; faking N identities means doing N streams of real useful labor over time, like waiting for comets — slow, rare, and unparallelizable. Sybil profit dies on the tundra of idle clones: identities that sit unused lose their standing to decay instead of banking it.
